subject: Post-demo recap: model shortlist, acceptance metrics, and proposed trial
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Patel <tara@helixbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: model shortlist, acceptance metrics, and proposed trial

Hi Tara — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clean plan to evaluate tradeoffs between HelixBank's baseline (HelixCore v2) and a couple of open-model alternatives.

1) Objective (what we agreed): short pilot to validate parity on your customer-facing FAQ & account-retrieval flows (approx 3k–6k daily queries during trial). Primary success criteria: quality parity with HelixCore v2 while reducing serving cost and keeping p95 latency within SLA.

2) Recommended shortlist to trial (we'll run side-by-side):
   - open-instruct-13B-8k (quantized q4) — low cost, strong instruction-following on short-context prompts; good for templated FAQ answers.
   - Llama-3-70B-q4f14 — higher-context reasoning; expect better concordance on multi-turn policy questions.
   - Baseline reference: HelixCore v2 (your in-house proprietary baseline) — we'll run identical prompt bundle + eval harness.

3) Acceptance metrics (proposed):
   - Accuracy / relevance on 50-shot human-verified prompt set: >= 92% (close parity band: +/- 3%).
   - Hallucination rate (measured via golden-ground truth extraction tasks): <= 3% absolute.
   - Latency p95 (99th for certain flows): <= 450ms for single-turn FAQ; <= 650ms for multi-turn (with KV cache enabled).
   - Regression tolerance: no more than 1 critical regression vs baseline on the 50-item safety/regulatory checklist.

4) Proposed trial scope and timeline:
   - 10 business day canary: 5k queries/day routed to each model variant (baseline + two open models).
   - Evaluation: automated metrics + small panel of 5 HelixBank reviewers for qualitative scoring.
   - Deliverables: benchmark CSV (attached), prompt set (attached), dashboard links and a readout.

5) Data & deployment notes:
   - For PII-sensitive flows we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment (VPC) so inference never transits public networks.
   - Quantized open models (q4) generally preserve quality but we should run a short sanity check on your edge-case prompts (we'll include these in the prompt bundle).

Next steps: if that looks good I can send an SOW + trial setup checklist. Would you prefer we start the canary next Tuesday (23rd) or wait until the week after?

Thanks — Michael

--
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
michael@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142
From: Tara Patel <tara@helixbank.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Joshi <samir.joshi@helixbank.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 09:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: model shortlist, acceptance metrics, and proposed trial

Thanks Michael — useful summary. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock dates: 

- Data residency & PII: for certain flows we cannot allow any inference outside our AWS accounts. Is Dedicated/Private the recommended path for the entire trial or can we run tokenized/scrubbed traffic on Hosted for the first pass?
- Cost: can you provide a ballpark cost delta (per-1M tokens) for the open models vs running HelixCore on our infra? Our finance partner needs that for the internal approval.
- Fine-tuning: we can't fine-tune on customer data — this is strictly inference-only. Will the open models give good enough out-of-the-box performance for our regulatory prompts?

If we can get your answers by EOD tomorrow we can aim at a 23rd start.

Best,
Tara

--
Tara Patel
Director, Digital Products — HelixBank
tara.patel@helixbank.com | +1 617-555-0199
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Patel <tara@helixbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Samir Joshi <samir.joshi@helixbank.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: model shortlist, acceptance metrics, and proposed trial

Tara — quick answers inline and a few operational asks.

- Data residency & PII: For any production-facing PII traffic we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). For the initial canary you have two safe options:
   a) Hosted with strong scrubbing: you route only tokenized/scrubbed prompts (we'll provide the scrubber patterns) — low friction but not suitable for full-scope regulatory checks.
   b) Dedicated trial: deploy the trial instances into a dedicated VPC (takes ~3 business days to provision once legal + networking greenlighted).

- Cost ballpark: (very approximate)
   - open-instruct-13B-q4: ~$120 per 1M tokens serving (hosted, amortized).
   - Llama-3-70B-q4f14: ~$420 per 1M tokens (hosted, higher memory footprint, better for long-context).
   - Running HelixCore v2 on your infra: depends heavily on utilization — we estimate equivalent throughput cost ~ $340 per 1M tokens given your GPU fleet utilization today.
   These are soft estimates; we'll provide a sample cost spreadsheet (attached) that maps to the expected 10-day canary.

- Fine-tuning: understood — no fine-tuning. We're proposing zero-shot / few-shot prompting with targeted prompt engineering + instruction templates in the attached prompt set. In our experience the open models above hit parity on templated FAQ and retrieval-augmented responses when given high-quality prompts and the right retrieval context.

Operational asks:
   - Please share a redacted sample of 200 prompts (we'll only use them in the eval harness).
   - Confirm whether you can sign the Trial SOW (I attached a draft link to HubSpot/docuSign).

If you prefer, we can run a tiny hosted canary (scrubbed) starting Aug 23 and run the Dedicated trial the following week. Which is easier for your infra team?

Thanks — I'll prep the SOW and attach the evaluation dashboard links.

--
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
michael@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: HelixBank trial — scoring rubric, risks, and commercial asks

Marissa / Neha — internal note after the call thread. Key points for commercial and CS planning: 

1) Scoring rubric (what we'll present to the customer):
   - Quantitative: accuracy (50-key prompts), hallucination rate, latency p95, tokens/call (cost proxy).
   - Qualitative: human panel score (5 reviewers) on clarity & regulatory alignment (scale 1–5).
   - Go/no-go is tied to: accuracy >= 92% AND no more than 1 critical regression on the safety checklist.

2) Risks / mitigation:
   - Risk: open models might show edge-case hallucination on regulatory language. Mitigation: add targeted prompt templates and retrieval augmentation for those prompts; escalate any critical regression to a manual review bucket.
   - Risk: customer insists on Dedicated start (network + legal gating). Mitigation: have infra request template ready; propose a staggered plan (hosted scrubbed -> dedicated).
   - Risk: cost negotiation — HelixBank may push for parity pricing vs their in-house run-rate. Mitigation: propose a time-limited pilot discount (we can offer a 25% pilot credit subject to SOW).

3) Commercial asks: please draft a short SOW (10-day trial, objectives + acceptance metrics) and a pilot credit clause. I want a clean signature path for Tara.

4) Tactical next steps:
   - Marissa: work up the SOW + pilot pricing + sample DocuSign envelope.
   - Neha: prep Dedicated provisioning checklist and an infra contact template (networking, KMS, audit logs requirements).
   - I'll follow up with HelixBank to collect the 200 redacted prompts and lock dates.

Putting this on our weekly pipeline review for Monday.

Thanks — Michael

--
Michael Grant
